Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Production Environments

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of their JPEG XS compression technology with 12G-SDI interfaces, allowing for reduced latency and increased signal integrity in live production environments. This development is particularly significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables more efficient and reliable transport of high-quality video signals. The technology is designed to work seamlessly with existing ST 2110 and NMOS-based systems.

Operational ROI

The introduction of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces can significantly reduce transmission costs and latency for live production environments. By compressing video signals in real-time, broadcasters can reduce the required bandwidth for transmission, resulting in cost savings of up to 50% compared to traditional uncompressed transmission methods. This technology affects the signal routing workflow step, allowing for simplified signal distribution and reduced hardware rack footprint. For example, a single 12G-SDI link can now carry multiple compressed video signals, reducing the need for multiple fiber optic connections.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as using multiple 3G-SDI links or fiber optic connections, the JPEG XS compression technology offers a more efficient and cost-effective solution. The reduced latency of 30% also enables more accurate synchronization of video signals, resulting in improved overall signal integrity. This is particularly important for live sports and event broadcasts, where timing and synchronization are critical.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces is designed to work with existing broadcast IT stacks, including ST 2110 and NMOS-based systems. The technology is compliant with relevant standards, including SMPTE ST 2110-22 and NMOS IS-05, ensuring secure and reliable operation. The use of JPEG XS compression also enables compliance with AES67 audio standards, allowing for synchronized audio and video transmission. Additionally, the technology is designed to work with RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocols, ensuring secure and reliable transmission of compressed video signals over IP networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The JPEG XS compression technology requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a compatible 12G-SDI interface, such as the intoPIX IP-cores. Engineers should also ensure that their systems are certified to the relevant standards, including SMPTE ST 2110-22 and NMOS IS-05.
  • Compatibility: The technology is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring compatibility with existing ST 2110 and NMOS-based systems. Engineers should verify that their systems are compatible with the JPEG XS compression format to ensure seamless integration.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standards, which are expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and 12G-SDI interfaces. This will ensure that their systems remain compliant and compatible with the latest developments in live production technology.

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces signals a significant shift towards more efficient and reliable live production environments. Engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and deployment of this technology to take advantage of the reduced latency and increased signal integrity it offers, and to ensure compliance with the latest standards and protocols.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables VideoAI to utilize NMOS protocol for device registration and connection management, streamlining IP-based media workflows with reduced latency and optimized bitrate allocation.
